summary: Intro discovery focused on NebulaWorks' compliance gate for vendor selection. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML + fine-grained RBAC, BYOK/KMS integration, audit log retention, and whether Redwood Hosted meets data residency and egress constraints vs Dedicated/Private. REDWOOD AE/SE outlined options and agreed to send docs and schedule a technical deep-dive for KMS integration and deployment sizing.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-22
Time: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Elliot Ramos (Redwood CSM); Samira Khan (CISO), Liam Ortega (Head of Platform), Priya Menon (Cloud Engineer), Diego Ruiz (Legal)

---- Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect) ----
Customer looking at Redwood for inference for internal AI features, primary gating is compliance and key management. Want to understand options for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and whether Redwood supports BYOK and HSM-backed KMS, plus audit log retention requirements.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side — maya from redwood, jordan our solutions engineer, elliot is here for cs and onboarding.
00:12 Speaker 2 (Samira): hi, samira here. thanks for doing this. we wanted a quick baseline on security posture before we get into any pilot specifics.
00:20 Speaker 3 (Liam): yeah, and i'll add, timeline is Q1 pilot target, procurement wants a vendor compliance snapshot.
00:28 Speaker 2 (Maya): great, can you share what your must-haves are? is SOC2 the big one, or residency etc?
00:34 Speaker 4 (Samira): SOC2 is required for procurement, plus we have two regional datasets that must remain within eu data centers for residency reasons. also need SSO - we use okta with SAML.
00:45 Speaker 1 (Jordan): ok, quick note — redwood hosted is multi-region and we support region pinning for model serving. we also support dedicated capacity and private deployments (vpc/on-prem) if you need isolated control.
00:59 Speaker 2 (Priya): when you say region pinning, do you manage keys? or can we use our own keys? we need BYOK for at-rest encryption of any persisted latent cache or logs.
01:08 Speaker 1 (Maya): we support customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private today; hosted supports envelope encryption with our provider KMS, but we do offer BYOK in private deployment and a BYOK roadmap for Dedicated — jordan can expand.
01:19 Speaker 3 (Jordan): yeah, for Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS via customer-owned key material, and for Private we support direct HSM integration and on-prem key stores. note: hosted by default is not BYOK for now, but we have options like bring-your-own-key for some enterprise accounts — depends on contract.
01:38 Speaker 4 (Diego): legal will need to see the KMS diagrams and key rotation policies. also audit logs: how long do you retain logs and can we export them to our SIEM?
01:47 Speaker 1 (Elliot): we retain operational audit logs by default 90 days, with longer retention available as an add-on. yes, exports to cloud storage or push to your SIEM via secure forwarder is supported. there can be variations between hosted and private deployments on retention SLAs.
02:05 Speaker 2 (Samira): 90 days by default — our compliance asks for 7 years for some PII access logs, that's a no-go unless we can get longer retention or full export.
02:17 Speaker 3 (Jordan): you can definitely offload logs to your own long-term storage — we provide signed, tamper-evident exports, but for hosted we need to confirm retention pricing. private/dedicated gives more control here.
02:30 Speaker 2 (Liam): okay, can we talk about SSO and RBAC mapping? we have groups in okta for devs, analysts, and restricted. we need fine grained role mapping to prevent model access for some groups.
02:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): Redwood supports SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC can be configured per project and per model route; jordan, do you want to add nuance on role scoping?
02:48 Speaker 3 (Jordan): sure — we have role templates for admin, dev, viewer, and can do custom roles. for sensitive model access we support per-route permissions and token scoping; note: for Hosted tokens we recommend short-lived tokens combined with SSO sessions. for Dedicated/Private you can run your own auth layer.
03:06 Speaker 2 (Priya): there's also KV cache concerns — some of our inputs may be cached at the prefix level, is that persisted? we need to know if cached kv is encrypted and if it leaves the region.
03:16 Speaker 1 (Jordan): good point — KV cache and prefix caches are stored in local storage attached to the serving runtime and encrypted at rest. for Hosted we manage that storage and it's region-aware; for Dedicated/Private you can control storage options and encryption keys.
03:30 Speaker 2 (Samira): any change of state that we should be worried about re: model outputs being stored? we need to show data lifecycle in audit.
03:40 Speaker 3 (Elliot): outputs are not persisted by default for Hosted unless you enable logs or request payloads be stored — we can disable persistence. for sessions we keep minimal telemetry. again, private/dedicated gives more control.
03:55 Speaker 4 (Diego): from a legal POV, what are the guarantees on subprocessor list and SOC2 scope? we need SOC2 type II with subprocessor attestations.
04:05 Speaker 1 (Maya): we are SOC2 Type II compliant — i'll send the report snapshot. we maintain a subprocessors list and can share the current roster under NDA.
04:15 Speaker 2 (Samira): are there any certifications around ISO 27001?
04:18 Speaker 3 (Jordan): yes, we have ISO 27001 certification for our control plane. i'll include cert scans and mapping docs.
04:26 Speaker 5 (Liam): curious about network egress and data flows — if we do hosted and route EU traffic to eu-region, do any tokens or telemetry go to us-west for control plane?
04:36 Speaker 1 (Maya): control plane metadata may be routed via our global control plane for management, but we support regional serving so tenant data stays in region. for stricter residency we recommend dedicated or private deployment.
04:48 Speaker 3 (Jordan): to add, we have an option for a local control plane in Private deployments so nothing leaves the VPC without customer-managed routes.
04:55 Speaker 2 (Priya): about KMS — are key operations performed in HSM or via cloud kms apis? we need attestation that key material never leaves our HSM.
05:05 Speaker 3 (Jordan): for Private we can integrate with your HSM and do crypto operations in your boundary. for cloud Dedicated we utilize cloud KMS and envelope encryption; key material does not leave cloud provider HSM when configured correctly. hosted uses our cloud KMS default unless BYOK negotiated.
05:22 Speaker 4 (Diego): ok so hosted may be tricky. procurement likely prefer hosted for speed but legal leans dedicated/private for control.
05:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): that's common — our customers often start hosted for dev and then move to Dedicated when they hit regulated scale.
05:38 Speaker 2 (Samira): what's the expected latency and cost hit for dedicated vs hosted? we have low-latency SLAs for some user-facing features.
05:46 Speaker 3 (Jordan): Dedicated gives predictability and lower per-token cost at scale; latency depends on sizing and region placement. Hosted can be fine for low volume, but if strict p99 latency is required Dedicated can be tuned. i'll put together a sizing sketch.
05:59 Speaker 4 (Liam): about audit logs again — do you support immutable logs or append-only tamper-evident storage?
06:06 Speaker 1 (Elliot): we support append-only export via signed manifests and hashes; for Private you can plug into your own ledger/storage for full immutability. Hosted we provide tamper-evident exports and SIEM integration.
06:20 Speaker 2 (Priya): would love to see a sample of the audit schema — fields, event types, who changed roles, who queried models etc.
06:28 Speaker 1 (Maya): jordan will follow up with sample schemas and log event types.
06:33 Speaker 3 (Jordan): note: there's some noisy telemetry we redact by default (PII). we also provide field-level redaction for logs.
06:44 Speaker 2 (Samira): ok next, data retention — our policy is 3 years for access logs and 7 years for PII access reviews. can you meet that?
06:53 Speaker 3 (Jordan): we can export logs to your archive for any retention you want, but on Hosted long-term retention may be an add-on cost. Private/Dedicated give direct, cheaper long-term retention options.
07:05 Speaker 1 (Maya): also a note about entitlements: token lifetime, revocation, and audit of API keys — we support token revocation and short-lived sessions via SSO.
07:16 Speaker 2 (Liam): do you have integrations for SIEMs like Splunk or Sumo? we use Splunk and need near real-time forwarding of security events.
07:23 Speaker 3 (Jordan): yes, Splunk, Datadog, Sumo are supported; we can forward via secure connectors and sign events.
07:33 Speaker 4 (Diego): on the contract front: indemnities re breach and subprocessors — we'll need to see sample contract language.
07:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): i'll coordinate legal to send standard contract redlines and subprocessors list after NDA.
07:46 Speaker 2 (Priya): what about model variants and fallback — if you do warm fallbacks to smaller models, do you ever send data to third-party models?
07:55 Speaker 3 (Jordan): by default we only serve models from our curated catalog unless a customer explicitly configures a third-party model. fallbacks are to compatible variants within the same catalog; no third-party model calls without config.
08:10 Speaker 2 (Samira): good. and about telemetry retention for prompts and outputs during debugging — can that be disabled?
08:18 Speaker 1 (Elliot): yes, debugging-level persistence is optional and can be turned off. we keep request/response for short windows unless enabled for evals.
08:27 Speaker 4 (Liam): procurement will want price bands — hosted vs dedicated vs private, and whether BYOK or long retention costs extra.
08:36 Speaker 1 (Maya): understood, i'll deliver a pricing matrix.
08:40 Speaker 2 (Samira): anything else on compliance? GDPR data subject requests — how do you handle deletions and right to be forgotten if data was used in model cache?
08:51 Speaker 3 (Jordan): we support delete-by-subject workflows and will scrub persisted items; for model weights there is no training on customer data in hosted inference. for any persisted cache we can remove entries and purge backups as part of DSAR processing — we'll provide the workflow.
09:04 Speaker 2 (Priya): would like a diagram that shows where data can land in all three deployment modes.
09:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): jordan will produce a deployment/data-flow diagram for hosted, dedicated, and private.
09:16 Speaker 4 (Diego): legal needs to know about incident response timelines and notifications. what's your SLO for breach notification?
09:24 Speaker 3 (Jordan): we notify within 72 hours for confirmed incidents and have an incident response team. also, for Dedicated/Private we can align SLAs contractually for notification windows.
09:36 Speaker 2 (Samira): ok this is helpful. could you also include a list of redwood subprocessors and a map of where they operate?
09:44 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, will include subprocessors and region map.
09:48 Speaker 2 (Liam): lastly, on the timeline — we want a pilot in Q1; what's a realistic kickoff?
09:55 Speaker 3 (Jordan): if we start contracting in Nov, we can do a dev pilot in January. we'll need a short POC scope and a small Dedicated pool or hosted sandbox depending on compliance needs.
10:08 Speaker 1 (Maya): recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO snapshot, subprocessors, KMS and BYOK diagrams, audit schema, pricing matrix, and propose a Dedicated sizing. schedule a technical deep-dive week of 2026-11-02.
10:22 Speaker 2 (Samira): perfect. agreed.
10:25 Speaker 1 (Elliot): action items noted. thanks all.

---- End of call ----

Call recap (human-readable):
Redwood and NebulaWorks covered core compliance requirements. NebulaWorks requires SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 evidence, SSO via Okta (SAML & SCIM), BYOK/HSM assurances for key operations, long-term audit log retention (3-7+ years via export), regional data residency for EU data, and contractual SLAs for incident notification. Redwood recommended Dedicated or Private deployments for strict residency and BYOK; Hosted may be acceptable for dev or non-regulated traffic. Next steps include Redwood sending compliance docs, a Dedicated sizing/pricing sketch, and scheduling an SE-led deep technical session for KMS/BYOK integration.
